description: RMSNorm, optionally fused with the residual add: x' = x + residual; out = x' * rsqrt(mean(x'^2) + eps) * weight; residual_out = x'. aiter rmsnorm2d / add_rmsnorm, sglang fused_add_rmsnorm, Triton variants.

rows.doc: tokens (times heads for a per-head q/k norm)

call: Many entries write out/residual in place (fused_add_rmsnorm overwrites x and residual). Clone the operands inside call() before invoking such an entry and return the written tensors as (out, residual_out); the driver checks that the caller's operands are unchanged after call().

timing.cache: x and residual come from the preceding kernel and are L2-warm in serving; read-evict makes this bandwidth-bound op look slower than served. Record it as the measured condition.

negative_controls: reduce the sum of squares over the first vector chunk only (or stop the row loop one chunk early): every output of the row rescales by a visible factor. Dropping eps is NOT a usable control: eps/mean(x^2) ~ 1e-6 sits below bf16 rounding
skip the weight multiply on the last vector chunk: error ~|y| on those columns
pitfalls: out's bound is one bf16 ulp (rtol 2^-7) against float64: a correct kernel rounds once (out) after an fp32 reduction; two roundings (normalize to bf16, then multiply weight) can land 2 ulp off. If the installed kernel does that, the task overrides the bound with a why rather than the candidate inheriting a loose one silently.
An in-place entry handed the same buffers across draws normalizes already-normalized data: call() must clone.
Per-head q/k norms (DeepSeek/GLM MLA) reshape (tokens, heads*dim) to (tokens*heads, dim): rows counts token-heads.
